issue: CSL valuation-date mismatch. Discounting anchors the valuation at 30 Jun 2026; net debt and share count are struck at 31 Dec 2025. Six months apart. Fable valued this at AUD 5–6/share; re-derived it is ±2%.
treatment: Two self-consistent repairs: (a) roll net debt forward, +1.7%; or (b) move the valuation date back with an H2-FY26 stub, −1.9%. (a) matches how DNL already does it.

issue: Terminal-share warning existed only in the industrial engine, so WBC (76.3%) and CSL (75.2%) — and WBC Stagflation at 84.5% — could not emit it.
treatment: Ported via a shared terminal_share_warning(); BankResult gained terminal_share_of_claim, both gained warnings. Six new assertions.

issue: Dead FX branch, translator.py:591 — both sides of the ternary return 1.0. Latent; DNL is AUD/AUD.
treatment: Raise NotImplementedError on the mismatch branch so the first genuine FX company fails loudly.

issue: CSL net_interest fields are populated but never read by the segment engine.
treatment: Resolves to delete: D-05 confirms CSL as FCFF/WACC, so interest belongs in the discount rate, not the cash flow.

issue: build_cfgs.py:697 prints "cfgs.json written", writes cfgs_gen.json.
treatment: Correct the message.

issue: translator.py:852–857 computes a gross-margin base then unconditionally overwrites it with 0.0.
treatment: Delete the dead branch.

issue: design/build_plan.html:167 still reads "Owner: Tara Reid".
treatment: Correct to Stephen. Already a known leftover in CLAUDE.md.

issue: WORKING_NOTES.md:44 says "Suite 113" while the file elsewhere says 122.
treatment: Partly disputed — it sits inside a dated 12 Aug historical entry where 113 was true at the time. Annotate as historical rather than rewrite.

issue: CSL discounts unlevered FCFF at the cost of equity, then deducts net debt — charges for the debt twice. Fable estimated +8–15% on EV; re-derived it is +21.5% to +26.6% on the per-share value, and it pushes CSL up, not down as the review's fix-order assumed. The largest open item in the project.
treatment: DECIDED 20 Aug 2026 (D-05): build a WACC on a target capital structure. Parameters proposed in csl_cost_of_debt_and_target_structure.md, awaiting confirmation (Q9).

issue: DNL terminal capitalises capex 7.0% against D&A 7.3% — the asset base runs down in perpetuity while revenue grows 2.5%. Worth −AUD 0.079/share (−2.6%). Fable's number checks out.
treatment: Bundle with the larger working-capital gap (M1) as one DNL reinvestment decision. Changes the audited workbook, not just the engine.

issue: Bank engine has no §15.5 CET1 constraint. Flat 0.75 payout in every world; book equity compounds at 2.6% p.a. against AIEA at 4.35%, so the implied capital ratio falls every year and the model never notices. Stagflation NPAT falls 57.5% with payout unchanged.
treatment: Warn-only check first (retained earnings vs AIEA growth × RWA density) — zero base-tie risk. Forced payout cut under stress as a separate second step. CET1 and RWA data already in wbc.yaml:538–568.

issue: Stub construction diverges from §7.2. The text says pro-rate the next full year; the engine pro-rates the base year. The engine ties the audited workbook, so the text is what is wrong.
treatment: Align the methodology text to the engine. Text edit, zero regression risk.

issue: CSL sits 93% above market — §16.3 requires the structural-reason treatment.
treatment: Price staleness parked by owner decision (D-19) — 15 June 2026 snapshot stands until Ben's feed returns. The §16.3 write-up follows once item 6 lands.

issue: β triangulation honoured in form, but DNL's peer dataset is flagged mock while the ratified β 1.10 narrative cites those peers.
treatment: Annotate the decision record to separate observed from awaited. Also: beta.mock is never read by gen_ui.py, so the mock warning is unconditional and will persist after Ben's feed lands — wire it.

issue: csl.yaml stores the same layer-2 judgment twice — broader than Fable's four items. Effectively the whole normalised_baseline scalar block mirrors segment_fcff, and only segment_fcff is read. Also duplicated beyond Fable's list: da_pct_revenue, working_capital_change, tax_rate, restructuring_cash_to_come, terminal_ebit_margin.
treatment: Delete the non-engine copies, keep the rationale prose beside the surviving copy.

issue: The ratchet cannot see intra-YAML duplication — check 3 scans code only. Second hole found: a value invented in code with no register source is also invisible (how the CSL broker literal survived).
treatment: Extend the lint with a same-file / cross-file duplicate-scalar check, plus a check for display values in code with no register source.

issue: §7.5 anchor-date discipline is enforced nowhere. This is the validator that would have caught item 1 automatically.
treatment: Warn when net debt, share count and discounting date are not struck at one date. Build alongside the item 1 repair.

issue: Layer-1/layer-2 split is clean where executed.
treatment: Independently spot-checked resolve_normalised_baseline and the WBC AIEA/NIM chain. Genuinely clean — agreed PASS.

issue: The Derivation layer covers the bridges but not the per-year build — all three engines emit revenue/EBIT/FCFF with empty inputs dicts, so the workbooks explain more than the engines can.
treatment: Finish the set: one step per P&L line per period, inputs populated. Low urgency, no risk.

issue: Only Muddle Through was pinned. The other five levels per company were asserted by ordering (WBC, CSL) or drivers (DNL), so a regression moving every level while preserving order passed silently.
treatment: All 18 pinned in test_scenario_goldens.py, flagged engine-owned not workbook-owned. Suite 122 → 146.

issue: The LibreOffice recalc tie runs ad hoc, not as a suite gate; _recalc.py is a regeneration script and is not collected by pytest.
treatment: Add an opt-in pytest marker so it can be run deliberately without making LibreOffice a hard suite dependency.

issue: Under-tested areas — engine_workbook.py (1,467 lines) has no coverage; __post_init__ validation errors untested.
treatment: Add workbook-builder and input-validation tests. Two of Fable's four claims are wrong: test_e2e_dnl_mt.py:103 does assert the §11.4.2 warning fires, and EquityBridge.from_anchor is exercised end-to-end with a pinned outcome.

issue: FiveForces has no model_validator — a block with neither entrants nor substitutes validates, and both naming generations can be supplied with contradictory ratings. bank_archetype and rivalry_subforces are untyped escape hatches.
treatment: One model_validator (one-of-each-force, reject dual-generation conflicts) plus a typed BankArchetype block.

issue: archetype=None falls back silently on file absence, so a typo'd archetype id degrades instead of raising.
treatment: Make the fallback conditional on an explicit segment_level_valuation marker.

issue: Standalone UI + base64 workbook architecture is sound; the "no JS engine port" decision held. One gap: no "reset all" for localStorage user scenarios.
treatment: Agreed PASS on the architecture. Add a reset-all control.

issue: Workbook discipline honoured with exceptions. DNL Equity bridge carries 14 literals (styled as inputs but off Assumptions); WBC Multiples!B3 hard-codes the market price.
treatment: Move the DNL bridge inputs onto Assumptions. For WBC the fix needs a step Fable missed: WBC's Assumptions sheet has no market-price row at all, so one must be added first.

issue: Headline sub-caption pvsub unused — the punchline isn't landed in 5 seconds.
treatment: Partly wrong — CSL's is populated. Do it for DNL and WBC: engine-sourced gap sentence.

issue: Metric card 4 is inconsistent — asymmetry for DNL/WBC, terminal share for CSL.
treatment: Show asymmetry for all three; move terminal share into the discount-rate panel beside the §11.4.2 warning.

issue: DNL's broker bar equals the market price (both 3.61) — the feed's target echoes spot.
treatment: Closed by owner decision 13 Aug: leave DNL alone until Ben's feed brings real coverage.

issue: Bar values show only the per-share number, no "% vs MT".
treatment: Add the delta beside each bar value — already computed for the narrative.

issue: The download button lives only inside detail panels, so the most persuasive traceability artefact is invisible until a reviewer drills down.
treatment: Persistent "Download audited workbook" in the header, sheet count from cfg.

issue: No provenance chip — the topnote reads as a disclaimer rather than a feature.
treatment: One-line engine/commit/data provenance under the header. Sell the one-source-of-truth story.

issue: Bars are click-only divs; the whole file has one aria-label; tab selection is border-colour only (WCAG 1.4.1 failure). The file is currently unusable by keyboard.
treatment: role/tabindex/Enter-Space/aria-label on bars; aria-pressed and a non-colour cue on tabs.

issue: Narrow-width overflow: fixed 122px label column, value label at calc(w% + 6px).
treatment: Move the value inside the bar above ~80% width. Partly wrong — the DCF workings table is already wrapped; the unwrapped one is the transitory-forces table.

issue: Slider moves silently swap the engine value for the reduced form.
treatment: Partly wrong — the override note already shows both values; the missing word is "approximation". The real problem Fable missed is bigger (see M5): the DCF panel is static but captioned as live.

issue: DNL has 8 explore tabs, WBC/CSL have 6 — reads as unfinished rather than data-blocked.
treatment: Add the missing tabs with an explicit "awaiting peer feed (Ben)" placeholder, which also advertises the dependency. Fable's five-forces cross-reference claim is wrong as stated — no company's UI panel has one; CSL's workbook has no five-forces sheet at all.

issue: Scenario narratives are buried one click deep.
treatment: Show the first sentence + "why it lands here" under the chart on bar selection.

issue: No onboarding for first-time reviewers.
treatment: Dismissible 3-step "how to read this" strip aimed at the feedback ask.

issue: No dedicated CSL market-gap panel.
treatment: Build it — but after items 6 and 10 land. Writing "why we differ" before knowing whether the gap is 93% or 140% is wasted work.

issue: No print/PDF stylesheet; the file prints poorly.
treatment: Worth doing if the prototype graduates.

issue: No side-by-side scenario comparison.
treatment: All the data is already in cfg. Nice-to-have.

issue: DNL assumes zero working capital in every explicit year and the terminal, while growing revenue 6.15% p.a. as an industrial manufacturer with receivables and inventory. Worth −AUD 0.14 to −0.27/share (−4% to −9%) — two to three times Fable's terminal-capex wedge. With item 7, DNL's reinvestment treatment is worth −7% to −11%, moving the discount to market from −15% to about −22%.
